title: Mai Mercado / Christiania 2016 — Article Contradiction and Framing Ledger
purpose: Audit contemporaneous and retrospective articles about the 2016 Mercado/Christiania case for source dependence, attribution drift, factual inconsistency, framing changes, omitted context, and unresolved conflicts with the Son's firsthand account.
core_rule: Do not treat repeated publication as independent confirmation. Track the first identifiable source for each proposition and distinguish direct quotation, reporter paraphrase, prosecution framing, court finding, Mercado statement, other-defendant testimony, and later retrospective shorthand.
firsthand_claims_to_test: Mercado deleted comments and later the whole thread after police/media involvement.
Some statements later attributed to the Son were written by other Facebook users.
Mercado's later recollection of the thread was inaccurate or conflated speakers/comments.
The central 'vil du gerne dø?' remark functioned as 'do you have a death wish / are you crazy?' in reply to another user's extreme comment.
The public/media story progressively lost the reply tree and speaker topology.

articles.title: Politiker får dødstrussel efter kontroversielt Facebook-opslag
key_points: Preserves Mercado's original 'gennemsmadrer hashboder' wording.
Describes broad backlash involving many users.
Frames at least one life-threat as reported to police.
Shows the controversy already contained multiple insults and speakers before the Son's remand hearing.
audit_notes: Important baseline because it predates the June 21 hearing coverage.
Use to reconstruct what was publicly known before courtroom paraphrases appeared.

articles.outlet: Ritzau republished by Avisen.dk / Local Eyes / Dagens
articles.title: Sønderjyde kræves fængslet for at true folketingsmedlem
articles.source_type: wire report citing TV2 and police
key_points: Mercado confirms to TV2 that she is the politician.
Police decline to identify the politician or specify conduct before the hearing.
Mercado says to TV2 that she did not make the police report.
Her follow-up describes police as having 'fjernede 37 hashboder' after the original post celebrated that police 'gennemsmadrer' the stalls.
She says she had not intended to provoke.
audit_notes: Framing shift: original forceful verb 'gennemsmadrer' becomes neutralized in her own follow-up as 'fjernede'.

Her statement that she did not intend to provoke sits alongside an original post that many contemporaries experienced as deliberately provocative; intention remains her self-report, not an objective fact.
The identity of the 'other' reporter is not supplied.

articles.title: 29-årig mand varetægtsfængslet i fire uger for trusler mod folketingsmedlem Mai Mercado
key_points: Reports that the defendant denied guilt and appealed remand.
Reports he acknowledged around fifteen Facebook posts/contributions.
Says individual posts were read aloud in court.
Publishes a compressed sequence of fragments joined by ellipses, including 'vil du gerne dø?' and knife/child/Jo Cox fragments.
audit_notes: This is one of the closest surviving sources to the hearing but is not a transcript.
Ellipses remove parent comments, addressees, intervening text, reply hierarchy and potentially speaker distinctions.
The fragmentary grammar ('jeg stikke...') indicates the printed text should not automatically be treated as verbatim Facebook transcription.
This article is a critical point where thread topology can be lost.

articles.title: Hashryger fængslet for dødstrusler mod K-politiker
key_points: Reports defendant's explanation that Mercado mocked cannabis users.
Prints three polished alleged statements and attributes them via JydskeVestkysten.
Says another Facebook user reported the case to police.
Prints the post-police 'consequences' statement.
Reports denial of guilt.
audit_notes: Attribution dependence is explicit: the incriminating quotations are not independently sourced by Ritzau but attributed to JydskeVestkysten.
The report says age 28, while same-day and later reports say 29: concrete factual inconsistency demonstrating metadata errors in the press chain.
The polished quotations are more syntactically complete than the local courtroom fragments, raising a provenance question about reconstruction versus verbatim text.
The phrase 'another Facebook user' remains unidentified and does not specify whether the report concerned the Son, another commenter, one particular Jo Cox remark, or the broader thread.

articles.title: Efter uge med drab, overfald og spytklat: Politikere efterlyser god tone – hos alle andre
key_points: Records the original forceful Christiania wording.
Notes that many people regarded it as glorification of brutal police conduct.
Records Mercado defending the word choice while simultaneously calling for civil tone.
Lists several extreme comments, including acid-bath, visit-at-night, sawn-apart and AIDS language, without establishing that all were written by one person.
audit_notes: Crucial evidence that the wider thread contained many extreme statements and multiple speakers.
Creates a concrete speaker-contamination risk when later articles discuss 'the threats' without preserving authorship per sentence.
The acid-bath statement is therefore part of the broader thread record, not presently primary-authenticated to the Son.

articles.title: 29-årig mand skal i fængsel for trusler mod Mai Mercado
key_points: Records five-month unconditional sentence and conviction on three of four counts.
Records prosecutor had requested six months.
Repeats the same three alleged statements again via JydskeVestkysten.
States flatly that after police visit the defendant 'threatened the politician again'.
audit_notes: Important semantic hardening: the earlier report gives the actual 'consequences' wording and notes the defendant's denial; the later article converts that disputed speech act into the declarative summary 'threatened again'.
This is an example of interpretation becoming narrative fact in later retelling.
The quotations remain source-dependent on the earlier JydskeVestkysten chain rather than newly authenticated by the judgment text in the article.

articles.title: Politiker glad for at Facebook-trusler fører til fængsel
key_points: Mercado says the case can now be put behind them.
She emphasizes the emotional effect of threats involving her child.
Article states that her whole family was threatened.
audit_notes: This article is valuable for separating Mercado's subjective fear/victim account from the attribution evidence itself.
It does not establish which defendant authored every family-related statement printed in the broader media environment.

articles.title: 18-årig dømt for Facebook-trusler mod folketingspolitiker
key_points: A separate 18-year-old woman is convicted over messages from the same broader controversy.
Her wording uses a third-party-danger structure: Mercado made people angry and should not feel safe with her child.
She acknowledges authorship and that the messages appeared threatening.
She receives 60 days suspended imprisonment.
audit_notes: Demonstrates conclusively that the wider event produced multiple defendants and multiple authors.
Useful comparison for speech-act structure, but her words are not textually identical to the Son's reported words.
Supports the need to attribute every quotation individually.

articles.title: Politikere får dødstrusler: Du skal ikke føle dig tryg
key_points: Mercado says people write asking whether she wants to die and that she should not feel safe in the street.
audit_notes: The plural 'de skriver' / people write is significant: by September Mercado is discussing repeated threats from multiple people, not necessarily one defendant.
Later readers can incorrectly back-project this generalized victim account onto the Son's individual authorship unless speaker boundaries are retained.

articles.title: 17-årig dømt for at true minister på livet
key_points: A different young defendant says in court that Mercado blocked him and reported him.
The case also arose from her June 17 Christiania post.
audit_notes: This does not contradict Mercado's claim that she did not report the Son unless the two reports are shown to be the same event.
It does establish that Mercado may have directly reported at least one other participant arising from the same original post.
Therefore blanket formulations such as 'Mercado never reported anyone' or 'Mercado reported the Son' are both too broad without report-level provenance.

articles.title: Husker du? 2016’s største shitstorms
key_points: Repeats the three alleged statements and explicitly cites JydskeVestkysten.
audit_notes: Demonstrates source multiplication rather than independent verification: later retrospectives reproduce the same attribution chain.
Should not be counted as new evidence for authorship.

articles.title: Mercado indtager børne- og socialministeriet
key_points: Retells the Christiania post and resulting convictions as part of Mercado's political biography when she becomes minister.
Places the threat story alongside her ideological/public profile.
audit_notes: Shows that the controversy became politically salient biographical material.
Does not establish that the controversy caused her ministerial appointment.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: Same-day wire coverage alternates between 28 and 29.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Concrete proof that even simple biographical metadata was not consistently transmitted; supports caution with more complex quotation provenance.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: SønderborgNYT prints ellipsis-linked fragments; later Ritzau/JydskeVestkysten-based reports present polished complete sentences.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Requires recovery of primary posts or judgment exhibits before treating later wording as exact Facebook text.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: Earlier articles give disputed wording; later judgment coverage summarizes that wording as 'threatened again'.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Legal/journalistic interpretation becomes embedded as event description.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: Reports repeatedly say another Facebook user reported the matter but do not identify the person or exact reported comment.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: The initial referral chain remains unresolved and should be reconstructed from police records if possible.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: A later separate 17-year-old says Mercado herself blocked and reported him, while Mercado had earlier said she did not make the report in the Son's case.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Different defendants may have entered police systems through different reports. All articles must be tied to exact defendant/report, not generalized into one story.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: Contemporary sources document many hostile commenters and at least multiple prosecutions; later summaries often discuss 'the threats' as one undifferentiated set.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Creates a plausible mechanism for reader-level or journalistic speaker conflation even without proving intentional fabrication.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: Original 'gennemsmadrer hashboder' becomes 'fjernede 37 hashboder' in the defensive follow-up while she says she did not intend to provoke.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: A documented shift in self-framing around the precipitating political act.

cross_article_anomalies.evidence: By September Mercado speaks broadly of people asking whether she wants to die and telling her not to feel safe, using plural/generalized language.
cross_article_anomalies.significance: Later recollections may aggregate multiple incidents. They should not be used to establish the Son's exact words without source-level linkage.

unverified_but_material_firsthand_allega.claim: Mercado deleted individual comments and later the whole Facebook thread after police/media involvement.
Mercado's recollection later assigned statements to the wrong speaker or otherwise became false.
Some published quotations flatly misattribute other users' comments to the Son.
needed_evidence: court exhibits identifying account/speaker per count

research_conclusions: There are demonstrable inconsistencies and framing transformations in the article ecosystem; this justifies a forensic audit.
Current public evidence is not sufficient to conclude intentional fabrication by Mercado or journalists.

The strongest present finding is provenance weakness: multi-speaker content becomes compressed, repeated through one source chain, and later presented with greater certainty than the earliest surviving reports warrant.
Claims about deletion and false recollection remain important because, if corroborated, they could explain why the surviving public record cannot reconstruct reply hierarchy or speaker attribution.
